correctness.rationale: Weighted matrix-tree Schur complement gives exact joint polynomial; a unique contraction bijection identifies the favorable Cayley-core event and yields the optimal TV formula. A uniform logarithmic expansion proves the cutoff, conditional occupancy factorial moments give independent Poisson collision and clique-edge defects, and exact Cayley two-point path counting plus TV transfer gives Rayleigh distance convergence. Replayed exact enumeration and separate symbolic determinants for 9 small graphs plus exact Cayley distance tests for orders 2–7 corroborate but do not replace the proof.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The exact forward generating formula alone is not original. Unlike a direct numerical evaluation or a restated marginal, the asserted distributional approximation identifies a geometric model on the full labeled tree space, with exact optimal TV distance and a sharp failure regime, and transfers a two-vertex distance limit. Its derivation uses additional structural inversion and singular occupancy analysis. No inspected stronger theorem was shown to imply the full geometric claim verbatim or as a stated special case. The 1994 work could contain related structure and remains a named residual risk.

originality.rationale: Originality is restricted to the geometric conditional Cayley-core law with exact TV and critical two-defect and distance consequences; the forward weighted degree generating identity is known from Klee–Stamps (2019) and earlier Clark, and not claimed as original. Relevant indexed records and three accessible primary texts did not demonstrate a covering structural TV theorem. residual_risks: Historical priority may overlap with Egecioglu–Remmel (1994), whose full text was not recovered.
Li–Chen–Yan (2023) full body was not accessible; its abstract is not a full-text exclusion.
Weighted degree polynomial and standard occupancy principles are prior knowledge; a reviewer may judge the structural cutoff a corollary of the classical multipartite enumerator.

value.rationale: A sharp whole-tree TV approximation, its iff square-root cutoff, independently identified Poisson defect mechanisms and Rayleigh clique-pair geometry address a natural asymptotic model-reduction gap for strongly imbalanced split graphs. Exact finite-size error quantifies when a uniform Cayley core can safely stand in for the full tree for arbitrary bounded observables; this is not an arbitrary finite census or a marginal degree recomputation.
